final_answer:
the sky appears blue during the day due to **rayleigh scattering**, where shorter wavelengths (blue/violet) scatter more strongly than longer wavelengths (red/orange) in the atmosphere. sunlight travels through less atmosphere when the sun is overhead, so scattered blue light dominates, filling the sky. violet isn’t perceived as strongly because our eyes are less sensitive to it, and some violet is absorbed by the upper atmosphere.

at sunset, sunlight passes through **more atmosphere** (a longer path). this scatters away most of the blue/violet light, leaving predominantly red/orange wavelengths to reach the observer. the sun itself appears red because only those longer wavelengths remain after scattering. thus, rayleigh scattering explains both the daytime blue sky and the sunset’s red/orange hues.
